docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to save the import report (if not specified, prints to terminal in tabular form).
  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To import all data sources from export file my_export.json into ProjectB:

dignacli import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

After the import, this command will also show a report of imported and skipped objects. Only new data sources will be imported into ProjectB. In order to find out which objects would be imported and skipped, you can use the command plan-import-ds

docs.title: plan-import-ds
docs.text: The plan-import-ds command in the digna CLI is used to import data sources into a target project and create an import report.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli plan-import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project to which the data sources would be imported.
  • EXPORT_FILE: The filename of the data sources export to be analyzed before the import.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to save the import report (if not specified, prints to terminal in tabular form).
  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To check which data sources would be imported and which would be skipped from export file my_export.json when imported into ProjectB:

dignacli plan-import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

This command will only show an import plan of objects to be imported and skipped.

docs.title: digna CLI Reference 2026.04
docs.text:
2026-04-08

This page documents the full set of commands available in digna CLI release 2026.04, including usage examples and options.

docs.title: help
docs.text:
The --help option provides information about available commands and their usage. There are two main ways to use this option:

  1. Displaying General Help:

    Use –help immediate after the keyword dignacl 

    dignacli --help

  2. Getting Help for Specific Commands:

    For detailed information about a specific command, append --help to that command. For example, to obtain help with the add-user command, run: 

    dignacli add-user --help

    ### output:

    • Command Description: Offers a detailed description of what the command does.
    • Syntax: Shows the exact syntax, including required and optional arguments.
    • Options: Lists any options specific to the command, along with their explanations.
    • Examples: Provides examples of how to execute the command effectively.

docs.title: check-config
docs.text: The check-config command is a utility within the digna CLI tool designed to test the configuration of digna. This command ensures that the digna components can find the needed configuration elements in the config.toml.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • --configpath, -cp: File or directory that contains the configuration. If omitted, ../config.toml will be used.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli check-config

Upon successful execution, the command outputs a confirmation of completeness of the configration.

If the configuration appears to be incomplete, the missing configuration elements will be listed.

docs.title: check-repo-connection
docs.text: The check-repo-connection command is a utility within the digna CLI tool designed to test the connectivity and access to a specified digna repository. This command ensures that the CLI can interact with the repository.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli check-repo-connection

Upon successful execution, the command outputs a confirmation of the connection, along with details about the repository: Repository version, Host, Database and Schema.

If the repository connection is not successful, check the config.toml file for correct configuration settings.

docs.title: version
docs.text: To check the installed version of dignacli, use the --version option.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli --version

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: dignacli version 2026.04

docs.title: logging options
docs.text:
By default, the console output of the digna commands is designed to be minimalistic. Most commands offer the possibility of providing additional information, using the following options:

-- verbose (-v) -- debug (-d) -- logfile (lf)

“verbose” and “debug” are defining the level of detail, whereas the “logfile” switch allows redirecting the output to be streamed to a file rather than the console window.

docs.title: add-user
docs.text: The add-user command in the digna CLI is used to add a new user to the digna system

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli add-user [OPTIONS] USER_NAME USER_FULL_NAME USER_PASSWORD

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• USER_NAME: The username for the new user (required).
  • USER_FULL_NAME: The full name of the new user (required).
  • USER_PASSWORD: The password for the new user (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --is_superuser, -su: Flag to designate the new user as an admin.
  • --valid_until, -vu: Sets an expiration date for the user account in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MI:SS. If not set, the account does not have an expiration date.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To add a new user with username jdoe, full name John Doe, and password password123:

dignacli add-user [OPTIONS] USER_NAME USER_FULL_NAME USER_PASSWORD

To add a new user and set an account expiration date: 

dignacli add-user jdoe "John Doe" password123 --valid_until "2024-12-31 23:59:59"

docs.title: delete-user
docs.text: The delete-user command in the digna CLI is used to remove an existing user from the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli delete-user USER_NAME

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • USER_NAME: The username of the user to be deleted (required). This is the only argument required by the command.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
dignacli delete-user jdoe

Executing this command will remove the user jdoe from the digna system, revoking their access and deleting their associated data and permissions from the repository.

docs.title: modify-user
docs.text: The modify-user command in the digna CLI is used to update the details of an existing user in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli modify-user <USER_NAME> <USER_FULL_NAME> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• USER_NAME: The username of the user to be modified (required).
  • USER_FULL_NAME: The new full name for the user (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --is_superuser, -su: Sets the user as a superuser, granting elevated privileges. This flag does not require a value.
  • --valid_until, -vu: Sets an expiration date for the user account in the format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MI:SS. If not provided, the account remains valid indefinitely.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To modify the full name of the user jdoe to “Johnathan Doe” and set the user as a superuser: 

dignacli modify-user jdoe "Johnathan Doe" --is_superuser

docs.title: modify-user-pwd
docs.text: The modify-user-pwd command in the digna CLI is used to change the password for an existing user in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli modify-user-pwd <USER_NAME> <USER_PWD>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• USER_NAME: The username of the user whose password is to be changed (required).
  • USER_PWD: The new password for the user (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To change the password for the user jdoe to newpassword123: 

dignacli modify-user-pwd jdoe newpassword123

docs.title: list-users
docs.text: The list-users command in the digna CLI displays a list of all users registered in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli list-users

Executing this command in the digna CLI will connect to the digna repository and list all users, showing their ID, username, full name, superuser status, and expiration timestamps.

docs.title: upgrade-repo
docs.text: The upgrade-repo command in the digna CLI is used to upgrade or initialize the digna repository. This command is essential for applying updates or setting up the repository infrastructure for the first time.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli upgrade-repo [options]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • --simulation-mode, -s: When enabled, this option runs the command in simulation mode, which prints the SQL statements that would be executed but does not actually execute them. This is useful for previewing changes without making any modifications to the repository.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To upgrade the digna repository, you can run the command without any options:

dignacli upgrade-repo
To run the upgrade in simulation mode (to see the SQL statements without applying them):

dignacli upgrade-repo --simulation-mode

This command is crucial for maintaining the digna system, ensuring that the database schema and other repository components are up to date with the latest version of the software.

docs.title: encrypt
docs.text: The encrypt command in the digna CLI is used to encrypt a password.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli encrypt <PASSWORD>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PASSWORD: The password that needs to be encrypted (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To encrypt a password, you need to provide the password as an argument. For instance, to encrypt the password mypassword123, you would use: 

dignacli encrypt mypassword123
This command outputs the encrypted version of the provided password, which can then be used in secure contexts. If the password argument is not provided, the CLI will display an error indicating the missing argument.

docs.title: generate-key
docs.text: The generate-key command is used to generate a Fernet key, which is essential for securing passwords stored in the digna repository.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli generate-key

docs.title: clean-up
docs.text: The clean-up command in the digna CLI is used to remove profiles, predictions, and traffic light system data for one or more data sources within a specified project. This command is essential for data lifecycle management, helping maintain an organized and efficient data environment by clearing outdated or unnecessary data.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli clean-up <PROJECT_NAME> <FROM_DATE> <TO_DATE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project from which data is to be removed (required). Using the keyword all-projects in this argument instructs digna to iterate over all existing projects and apply this command.
  • FROM_DATE: The start date and time for the data removal. Acceptable formats include %Y-%m-%d, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S, or %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S (required).
  • TO_DATE: The end date and time for the data removal, following the same formats as FROM_DATE (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name, -tn: Limits the clean-up operation to a specific table within the project.
  • --table-filter, -tf: Filters to limit the clean-up to tables containing the specified substring in their names.
  • --timing, -tm: Displays the time duration of the clean-up process after completion.
  • --help: Displays help information for the clean-up command and exits.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To remove data from the project ProjectA between January 1, 2023, and June 30, 2023:

dignacli clean-up ProjectA 2023-01-01 2023-06-30

To remove data only from a specific table named Table1:

dignacli clean-up ProjectA 2023-01-01 2023-06-30 --table-name Table1

This command helps in managing data storage and ensuring that the repository only contains relevant information.

docs.title: remove-orphans
docs.text: The remove-orphans command in the digna CLI is used for house-keeping in the digna repository. When a user deletes projects or data sources, the profiles and predictions remain in the repository. With this command, such orphaned rows will be removed from the repository.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli list-projects

docs.title: list-projects
docs.text: The list-projects command in the digna CLI is used to display a list of all available projects within the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli list-projects

This command is especially useful for administrators and users managing multiple projects, providing a quick overview of the available projects in the digna repository.

docs.title: list-ds
docs.text: The list-ds command in the digna CLI is used to display a list of all available data sources within a specified project. This command is useful for understanding the data assets available for analysis and management in the digna system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli list-ds <PROJECT_NAME>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project for which the data sources are being listed (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To list all data sources in the project named ProjectA:

dignacli list-ds ProjectA

This command provides users with an overview of the data sources available in a project, helping them to navigate and manage the data landscape more effectively.

docs.title: inspect
docs.text: The inspect command in the digna CLI is used to create profiles, predictions, and traffic light system data for one or more data sources within a specified project. This command helps in analyzing and monitoring data over a defined period. After completion of the inspection, the value of the calculated traffic light system is returned: - 0: OK - 1: INFO - 2: WARNING

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli inspect <PROJECT_NAME> <FROM_DATE> <TO_DATE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project for which data is to be inspected (required). Using the keyword all-projects in this argument instructs digna to iterate over all existing projects and apply this command.
  • FROM_DATE: The starting date and time for the data inspection. Acceptable formats include %Y-%m-%d, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S, or %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S (required).
  • TO_DATE: The ending date and time for the data inspection, following the same formats as FROM_DATE (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name, -tn: Limits the inspection to a specific table within the project.
  • --table-filter, -tf: Filters to inspect only tables containing the specified substring in their names.
  • --enable_notification, -en: Enables the sending of notifications in case of alerts.
  • --bypass-backend, -bb: Bypass backend and run inspection directly from CLI (for testing purposes only!).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To inspect data for the project ProjectA from January 1, 2024, to January 31, 2024:

dignacli inspect ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31

To inspect only a specific table and force recalculation of predictions:

dignacli inspect ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31 --table-name Table1 --force-prediction
This command is useful for generating updated profiles and predictions, monitoring data integrity, and managing alert systems within a specified project timeframe.

docs.title: inspect-async
docs.text: The inspect-async command in the digna CLI is used to create profiles, predictions, and traffic light system data for one or more data sources within a specified project. This command helps in analyzing and monitoring data over a defined period. In contrast to the inspect-async command, this does not wait for the completion of the inspection. Instead, it returns the request id for the submitted inspection request. To query the progress of the inspection process, use the command inspect-status

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli inspect-async <PROJECT_NAME> <FROM_DATE> <TO_DATE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project for which data is to be inspected (required). Using the keyword all-projects in this argument instructs digna to iterate over all existing projects and apply this command.
  • FROM_DATE: The starting date and time for the data inspection. Acceptable formats include %Y-%m-%d, %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S, or %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S (required).
  • TO_DATE: The ending date and time for the data inspection, following the same formats as FROM_DATE (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name, -tn: Limits the inspection to a specific table within the project.
  • --table-filter, -tf: Filters to inspect only tables containing the specified substring in their names.
  • --enable_notification, -en: Enables the sending of notifications in case of alerts.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To inspect data for the project ProjectA from January 1, 2024, to January 31, 2024:

dignacli inspect-async ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31

docs.title: inspect-status
docs.text: The inspect-status command in the digna CLI is used to check the progress of an asynchronous inspection based on the request ID.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli inspect-status <REQUEST ID>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • REQUEST_ID: The request id returned by the inspect-async command

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To check the progress of an inspection with request ID 12345:

dignacli inspect-status 12345

docs.title: inspect-cancel
docs.text: The inspect-cancel command in the digna CLI is used to cancel inspections based on the request ID or it can be used to cancel all current requests.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text:
dignacli inspect-cancel <REQUEST ID>
dignacli inspect-cancel --killall

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • REQUEST_ID: The request id returned by the inspect-async command

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To cancel the inspection with request ID 12345:

dignacli inspect-cancel 12345

To cancel all requests that are currently running or pending:

dignacli inspect-cancel --killall

docs.title: export-ds
docs.text: The export-ds command in the digna CLI is used to create an export of data sources from the digna repository. By default, all data sources from a given project will be exported.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli export-ds <PROJECT_NAME> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project from which the data sources will be exported.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table_name, -tn: Export a particular data source from a project.
  • --exportfile, -ef: Specify the filename for the export.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To export all data sources from the project named ProjectA:

dignacli export-ds ProjectA

This command exports all data sources from ProjectA as a JSON document that can be imported to another project or digna repository.

docs.title: import-ds
docs.text: The import-ds command in the digna CLI is used to import data sources into a target project and create an import report.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project to which the data sources will be imported.
  • EXPORT_FILE: The filename of the data sources export to be imported.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to save the import report (if not specified, prints to terminal in tabular form).
  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To import all data sources from export file my_export.json into ProjectB:

dignacli import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

After the import, this command will also show a report of imported and skipped objects. Only new data sources will be imported into ProjectB. In order to find out which objects would be imported and skipped, you can use the command plan-import-ds

docs.title: plan-import-ds
docs.text: The plan-import-ds command in the digna CLI is used to import data sources into a target project and create an import report.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: dignacli plan-import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [options]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project to which the data sources would be imported.
  • EXPORT_FILE: The filename of the data sources export to be analyzed before the import.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to save the import report (if not specified, prints to terminal in tabular form).
  • --output-format, -f: Format to save the import report (json, csv).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To check which data sources would be imported and which would be skipped from export file my_export.json when imported into ProjectB:

dignacli plan-import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

This command will only show an import plan of objects to be imported and skipped.

docs.title: digna CLI Reference 2026.06
docs.text:
2026-09-05

This page documents the full set of commands available in digna CLI release 2026.06, including usage examples and options.

The executable is called digna.

docs.title: Overview & Syntax
docs.text:
The release 2026.06 CLI uses a structured, category-based command hierarchy:

digna [GLOBAL_OPTIONS] <COMMAND_CATEGORY> <SUBCOMMAND> [OPTIONS] [ARGUMENTS]

version and serve are single commands without a subcommand:

digna [GLOBAL_OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [OPTIONS] [ARGUMENTS]

docs.title: Global Options
docs.text:
The following global options apply across all commands:

  • --help, -h: Display help information for the CLI or a specific command category or subcommand.
  • --stacktrace: Display the full error chain on failure instead of only the top-level message.

--stacktrace is a global option in the strict sense: it has to be given before the command category, not after it.

digna --stacktrace repo check     # correct
digna repo check --stacktrace     # rejected: unknown argument

There is no --version flag. Use the version command instead.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Most commands need a readable, valid config.toml; some additionally require a valid license. The following table records what each command category loads before it does anything:

Command category Needs config.toml Needs a valid license version no no config check no (it is what the command reports on) no license check no it is the check crypt yes no serve yes no project yes no user yes yes inspection yes yes repo yes yes

Where a license is required, both its signature and its expiry date are checked, and the command aborts before touching the repository if either fails.

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
• 0: the command succeeded.
  • 1: the command failed. The error message is written to stderr, prefixed with Error:.

docs.title: help
docs.text:
The --help option provides information about available command categories, subcommands, and options:

  1. Displaying General Help: 

    digna --help

  2. Getting Help for Specific Categories and Commands: 

    digna user --help
digna user add --help

Output Includes: - Command Description: Summary of the command purpose. - Syntax: Required and optional arguments. - Options: Flags and parameters specific to the command.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
The version command prints the installed digna release. It reads no configuration and validates no license, so it also works on an installation whose config.toml or license is missing or invalid.

The release version is independent of the repository schema version reported by repo check.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna version

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: 2026.06

docs.title: config check
docs.text:
The config check command validates the configuration file (config.toml), verifying that all mandatory sections and settings are present and properly formatted. Each section is validated on its own, so a broken [app] section does not hide the state of [repo].

The sections reported are:

  • App config ([app])
  • Repository config ([repo])
  • Base config ([base])
  • Logging config ([logging])
  • Encryption config ([encryption])
  • OIDC config(s) (oidc_clients) — optional; an absent key passes, a present but malformed list fails

The command deliberately does not load the application configuration the way the other commands do, so it can diagnose a config.toml that would stop digna from starting at all.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna config check [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --configpath, -c: Path to the configuration file, or to a directory containing config.toml (defaults to ./config.toml).
  • --json: Output the validation report as JSON. Takes precedence over --quiet.
  • --quiet, -q: Suppress the report and rely solely on the exit code.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
digna config check

Validate a specific configuration file and format output as JSON: 

digna config check --configpath /etc/digna/config.toml --json

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
Configuration validation report (source: config.toml):
 - App config: OK
 - Repository config: OK
 - Base config: OK
 - Logging config: OK
 - Encryption config: FAILED
    missing field `aes_gcm_key`
 - OIDC config(s): OK

Overall: FAILED

A missing file or a TOML syntax error leaves nothing to validate section by section and is reported as a single error instead of a report, regardless of --quiet or --json.

docs.title: repo check
docs.text:
The repo check command tests the database connection and verifies repository installation and version. It fails if the configured schema does not exist, or if it exists but holds no digna repository.

The version reported is the version of the repository schema, which is versioned separately from the digna release printed by version.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna repo check

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: Repo version 3.0.0 installed

docs.title: repo install
docs.text:
The repo install command installs a new digna repository into the schema configured in config.toml, creating all required sequences, tables, indices, constraints, and initial records.

The schema itself is not created by this command — it has to exist beforehand. The command also refuses to run if a repository is already installed in that schema, and points at repo upgrade if the installed version is an older one.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna repo install

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
Installing repo version 3.0.0
✅ Sequences created.
✅ Tables and Indices created.
✅ Constraints created.
✅ Records inserted.
✅ Repo version 3.0.0 successfully installed.

docs.title: repo upgrade
docs.text:
The repo upgrade command applies database schema migrations to bring an existing repository up to the version expected by the installed release. Upgrades are applied one version hop at a time along a fixed upgrade path, and each completed hop is recorded in the repository.

If the repository is already at the expected version, the command reports that no upgrade is needed and makes no changes.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna repo upgrade

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
Upgrading from 2.3.1 to 2.3.2...
Upgrading from 2.3.2 to 3.0.0...
✅ Repo successfully upgraded to version 3.0.0.

docs.title: crypt gen-key
docs.text: The crypt gen-key command generates a new AES-GCM encryption key, for use as the encryption key in config.toml. A loadable config.toml must already be present, even though the generated key does not depend on it.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna crypt gen-key

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: Encryption key: <base64-encoded key>

docs.title: crypt encrypt
docs.text: The crypt encrypt command encrypts a string (such as a database password) using the AES-GCM key configured in config.toml, and prints the ciphertext.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna crypt encrypt <VALUE>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • VALUE: The plaintext string to encrypt (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna crypt encrypt mysecretpassword

docs.title: crypt decrypt
docs.text: The crypt decrypt command decrypts an AES-GCM encrypted string using the key configured in config.toml, and prints the plaintext.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna crypt decrypt <VALUE>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • VALUE: The encrypted ciphertext string to decrypt (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna crypt decrypt "encrypted_string_here"

docs.title: user add
docs.text: The user add command creates a new user account in the digna repository. The command fails if a user with the given email address already exists.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna user add <EMAIL> <PASSWORD> <DISPLAY_NAME> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• EMAIL: The email address for the user (required).
  • PASSWORD: The initial password for the user (required).
  • DISPLAY_NAME: The full display name of the user (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • --admin, -a: Create the user with administrator (superuser) privileges.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
digna user add jdoe@example.com "SecurePass123!" "John Doe"

To create an administrator account: 

digna user add admin@example.com "AdminPass123!" "Admin User" --admin

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: User created with ID: 42

docs.title: user list
docs.text: The user list command lists all registered users in tabular format with ID, email, display name, and administrator flag.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna user list

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
ID                   EMAIL                          DISPLAY NAME                   ADMIN
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
42                   jdoe@example.com               John Doe                       false
43                   admin@example.com              Admin User                     true

docs.title: user modify
docs.text:
The user modify command updates the display name and administrator privileges of an existing user account, identified by email address.

Both the display name and the administrator flag are always written. --admin is a switch, not a value: omitting it revokes administrator privileges, so pass it whenever the user should keep or gain them.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna user modify <EMAIL> <DISPLAY_NAME> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• EMAIL: The email of the user to modify (required).
  • DISPLAY_NAME: The updated display name (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --admin, -a: Grant administrator privileges. Omit to revoke them.
  • --valid-until, -v: Accepted for compatibility but not currently applied. Passing it prints a warning and changes nothing.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna user modify jdoe@example.com "Johnathan Doe" --admin

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: User jdoe@example.com modified successfully

docs.title: user modify-pwd
docs.text: The user modify-pwd command updates the password for an existing user account.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna user modify-pwd <EMAIL> <PASSWORD>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• EMAIL: The email of the user whose password is to be updated (required).
  • PASSWORD: The new password (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna user modify-pwd jdoe@example.com "NewSecurePass456!"

docs.title: user delete
docs.text: The user delete command removes a user account from the system.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna user delete <EMAIL>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • EMAIL: The email of the user to delete (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna user delete jdoe@example.com

docs.title: project list
docs.text: The project list command lists all available projects in the repository, showing their ID, name, and description.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna project list

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
ID                   NAME                           DESCRIPTION
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7                    ProjectA                       Sales data quality
8                    ProjectB                       Finance data quality

docs.title: project list-ds
docs.text: The project list-ds command lists all data sources associated with a given project, displaying their ID, name, kind, schema, and table name.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna project list-ds <PROJECT_NAME>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project whose data sources should be listed (required). The name must match exactly.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna project list-ds ProjectA

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
ID                   NAME                           KIND            SCHEMA               TABLE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
101                  orders                         Table           sales                orders
102                  customers                      Table           sales                customers

docs.title: project export-ds
docs.text:
The project export-ds command exports data sources from a project into a JSON document.

If neither --table-name nor --table-id is given, all data sources of the project are exported.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna project export-ds <PROJECT_NAME> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • PROJECT_NAME: The name of the project to export data sources from (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name, -n: Data source names to export. Multiple names can be given separated by spaces.
  • --table-id, -i: Data source IDs to export. Multiple IDs can be given separated by spaces.
  • --exportfile, -f: Path to save the exported data sources to (default: data_sources_export.json).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To export all data sources from ProjectA: 

digna project export-ds ProjectA --exportfile my_export.json

To export specific tables: 

digna project export-ds ProjectA --table-name users orders -f users_orders_export.json

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: Successfully exported 2 data source(s) to users_orders_export.json

docs.title: project import-ds
docs.text: The project import-ds command imports data sources from an export file into a target project, and reports per object what was created, updated, or skipped.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna project import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: Target project name to import into (required).
  • EXPORT_FILE: Path to the JSON export file (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to write the import report to. Without it, the report goes to stdout.
  • --output-format, -f: Format of the import report — table, json, or csv (default: table).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
digna project import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

To capture a machine-readable report: 

digna project import-ds ProjectB my_export.json --output-format json --output-file import_report.json

The report covers four object levels — data source, data set definition, attribute, and validation rule — each with its import action, result, resulting object ID, and any additional information.

docs.title: project plan-import-ds
docs.text: The project plan-import-ds command previews a data source import into a target project, showing which objects would be created, updated, or skipped, without changing anything. It takes the same export file and the same reporting options as project import-ds, and adds a step number per planned object.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna project plan-import-ds <PROJECT_NAME> <EXPORT_FILE> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: Target project name (required).
  • EXPORT_FILE: Path to the export file (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --output-file, -o: File to write the import plan to. Without it, the plan goes to stdout.
  • --output-format, -f: Format of the import plan — table, json, or csv (default: table).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna project plan-import-ds ProjectB my_export.json

docs.title: inspection run
docs.text:
The inspection run command creates an inspection request for a project and a date range, and then — depending on the options given — either waits for it, returns immediately, or runs it in-process.

The three execution modes are:

  • Default (no flag): the request is queued for the backend, and the CLI polls it every two seconds, printing task progress until the inspection reaches a final state. A running digna serve is required, otherwise nothing picks the request up.
  • --async-mode: the request is queued and its ID is printed immediately. Use inspection status to follow it.
  • --bypass-backend: the inspection is executed by the CLI process itself and is not queued, so no running server is needed.

--async-mode and --bypass-backend are mutually exclusive.

In every mode the command ends with a non-zero exit code if the inspection did not complete successfully.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna inspection run <PROJECT_NAME> <START_DATE> <END_DATE> [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text:
• PROJECT_NAME: The target project name (required). The name must match exactly.
  • START_DATE: Start date of the date range in YYYY-MM-DD format (required).
  • END_DATE: End date of the date range in YYYY-MM-DD format (required).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --table-name: Restrict the inspection to a single data source of the project, given by its data source name. Without it, all data sources of the project are inspected.
  • --async-mode: Queue the inspection and print the request ID instead of waiting for it. Cannot be combined with --bypass-backend.
  • --bypass-backend: Run the inspection directly in the CLI process instead of queueing it for the backend. Cannot be combined with --async-mode.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
digna inspection run ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31

To submit an asynchronous inspection: 

digna inspection run ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31 --async-mode

To inspect a single data source: 

digna inspection run ProjectA 2024-01-01 2024-01-31 --table-name orders

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
Default mode: 

Inspection request submitted. Waiting for completion (Request ID: 1024)...
Progress: 3/10 tasks completed (0 failed)
Progress: 10/10 tasks completed (0 failed)
Inspection completed successfully.
Inspection successful for project: ProjectA

Asynchronous mode: 

Inspection request submitted successfully. Request ID: 1024

docs.title: inspection status
docs.text: The inspection status command queries the state and task progress of an inspection request by its request ID.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna inspection status <INSPECTION_REQUEST_ID>

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • INSPECTION_REQUEST_ID: The numerical inspection request ID (required).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna inspection status 1024

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
Inspection Request ID: 1024
Status: Running
Project ID: 7
Date Range: 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-31
Progress: 3/10 tasks completed (0 failed)

docs.title: inspection abort
docs.text: The inspection abort command requests cancellation of running or pending inspection requests. It records a stop event for each affected request; the backend acts on it, so an abort is a request to stop rather than an immediate kill.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna inspection abort [INSPECTION_REQUEST_ID] [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: • INSPECTION_REQUEST_ID: The inspection request ID to abort. Required unless --killall is given.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • --killall: Abort all currently running and pending inspection requests. Takes precedence over a request ID given alongside it.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
To abort a specific request: 

digna inspection abort 1024

To abort all active and queued inspections: 

digna inspection abort --killall

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
--killall reports what it did; aborting a single request produces no output and reports success through its exit code. 

All running and pending inspections have been aborted.

docs.title: license check
docs.text: The license check command validates license.toml, verifying its signature against the public key shipped with the installation and checking that it has not expired. It reads no application configuration, so it also works before config.toml is set up.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna license check

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text:
License is valid

An invalid signature and an expired license are reported as distinct errors, both with exit code 1.

docs.title: serve
docs.text:
The serve command launches the digna REST API server along with the background inspection scheduler and inspection manager. At startup it also fails any inspection the repository still records as running, since nothing can have survived from an earlier process.

The command runs in the foreground until it is stopped.

docs.title: Command Usage
docs.text: digna serve [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• --address: Network address to bind the API server to (default: 127.0.0.1).
  • --port: Port number to listen on (default: 8000).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: digna serve --address 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

docs.title: Example Output
docs.text: Server running on http://0.0.0.0:8000

docs.title: digna CLI Reference – Introduction | digna Documentation
Purpose of the Command Line Interface (CLI)
docs.text: The digna Command Line Interface (CLI) is a powerful tool designed to streamline interactions with the digna platform. It provides a text-based interface that allows users to perform a wide range of tasks efficiently, without the need for a graphical user interface.

docs.title: Key Features:
docs.text:
• Efficiency and Flexibility: The CLI enables quick execution of commands, improving productivity.
  • Automation: Supports scripting to automate repetitive tasks.
  • Remote Access: Manage digna resources from anywhere.
  • Consistency and Reliability: Ensures reliable operations with documented, version-controlled commands.
  • Scalability: Handles large-scale operations for enterprise tasks.
  • Learning and Mastery: Provides deeper understanding of digna's functionality.
  • Integration with Other Tools: Seamlessly integrates with automation tools like Control-M, UC4, AutomateNOW!

docs.title: Installation Instruction for Windows
docs.text:
To get started, follow the steps outlined below to extract the necessary files, deploy the dignacli folder, and configure your connection to the digna repository. Ensure you have your repository credentials and any required configuration details ready before you begin.

  1. Extracting the digna CLI:
  2. Obtain the .zip file containing the digna CLI.

  3. Unzip the file to your desired directory.

  4. Deploying the dignacli Folder:

  5. Copy the dignacli folder to your preferred installation location (e.g., C:\Program Files\***digna***).

  6. Configuring config.toml:

  7. Check for config.toml inside dignacli.
  8. Rename config_template.toml to config.toml if needed and configure it using the provided documentation.

docs.title: Source Connector for Azure Synapse Analytics
docs.text:
This guide describes how to configure digna to connect to Azure Synapse Analytics using either the native Python connector or the ODBC driver. It supports both serverless and dedicated SQL pools.

This configuration refers to the screen "INTEGRATIONS" → "DB CONNECTIONS" → "+ ADD DB CONNECTION".

docs.title: Native Python Driver
docs.text:
Library: pymssql Supported Authentication: Password-based authentication only

For other authentication methods, please use the ODBC driver.

docs.title: digna Configuration (Native Driver)
docs.text:
Provide the following information in the "Create Database Connection" screen:

Name:               Name of the connection. This is used for referencing the connection in other screens.
Technology:         MS SQL Server
Host Address:       <synapse-workspace>[-ondemand].sql.azuresynapse.net
Host Port:          Port number, e.g. 1433
Database Name:      Database name
User Name:          Database user name
User Password:      Password for the user
Profiling Mode:     The profiling mode determines how digna processes data and calculates metrics:
                    - Standard: Metrics are calculated directly on the source tables without copying the data.
                    - Permanent: Data for the inspected day is copied into a permanent table, and metrics are calculated on the copied data.
                    - Session: Data is copied into a session or temporary table, and metrics are calculated on this temporary data.
                    For serverless SQL pool, only "Standard" is supported.
Work Schema Name:   When using "Permanent" profiling mode, work tables will be placed in this schema.
Use ODBC:           Disabled (default)

docs.title: ODBC Driver
docs.text: The ODBC driver may support a broader range of authentication and connectivity options. This section focuses on password-based authentication using the driver ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server.

docs.title: 1. Install the ODBC Driver
docs.text: Install the driver ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server (or similar) by following the vendor’s official installation guide.

docs.title: 2. Configure the ODBC Data Source
docs.text: Follow these steps to configure a new ODBC data source using password-based authentication:

docs.title: Step 1
docs.text:
Fill out the "Server" field. Use the name of the synapse workspace and extend it with ".sql.azuresynapse.net. Attention, if you want to connect using a serverless SQL pool, make sure to include "-ondemand" as shown in below screenshot.

Click the Next > button.

docs.title: Step 2
docs.text:
Choose the authentication method (e.g. username and password) and provide the required data.

Click the Next > button.

docs.title: Step 3
docs.text: Choose the ANSI compliant settings then click the Next > button.

docs.title: Step 4
docs.text: You can leave the default settings or choose options as needed and click the Finish button.

docs.title: Step 5
docs.text: Now click the Test datasource button.

docs.title: Step 6
docs.text:
When you receive the success screen, ODBC is configured properly.

Now you can configure digna to use the ODBC connection, either with a DSN (Data Source Name) or a DSN-less setup.

docs.title: digna Configuration
docs.text:
In the "Create Database Connection" screen, provide the following:

Name:               Name of the connection. This is used for referencing the connection in other screens.
Technology:         MS SQL Server
Database Name:      Database that contains the source schemata
Profiling Mode:     The profiling mode determines how digna processes data and calculates metrics:
                    - Standard: Metrics are calculated directly on the source tables without copying the data.
                    - Permanent: Data for the inspected day is copied into a permanent table, and metrics are calculated on the copied data.
                    - Session: Data is copied into a session or temporary table, and metrics are calculated on this temporary data.
                    For serverless SQL pool, only "Standard" is supported.
Work Schema Name:   When using "Permanent" profiling mode, work tables will be placed in this schema.
Use ODBC:           Enabled

name: "UID",        value: "your database user"

The DSN must match the name defined in your ODBC driver configuration.
